messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Ozempic Dosing Information:
Ozempic Injection Recommended Dosage:
- Start Ozempic with a 0.25 mg subcutaneous injection (injection under the skin) once weekly for 4 weeks. The 0.25 mg dosage is intended for treatment initiation and is not effective for glycemic control.
- After 4 weeks on the 0.25 mg dosage, increase the dosage to 0.5 mg once weekly.
- If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 0.5 mg dosage, the dosage may be increased to 1 mg once weekly.
- If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 1 mg dosage, the dosage may be increased to 2 mg once weekly. The maximum recommended dosage is 2 mg once weekly.
- Administer Ozempic once weekly, on the same day each week, at any time of the day, with or without meals.
- The day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary, as long as the time between two doses is at least 2 days (>48 hours).
Triplet: ["Semaglutide", "has recommended dose after 4 weeks on 1 mg", "2 mg once weekly"]

The relation 'has recommended dose after 4 weeks on 1 mg' in the triplet is defined as 'After at least 4 weeks on a 1 mg dose, the subject drug may be increased to the dose specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has duration of treatment': The subject drug is typically taken for the length of time specified by the object entity.
B. 'has half life': The subject drug remains in the body for the duration specified by the object entity.
C. 'has strength': The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
D. 'has onset of effect': The subject drug starts to work or shows its effect within the time period specified by the object entity.
E. 'has typical weight gain': The subject drug is associated with a typical amount of weight gain specified by the object entity over a given time period.
F. None of the above.
